column1: # Macros Emacs' *own source headers* define, which config.h alone cannot decide, and which
# the frozen `#if` evaluator therefore had to be told about (tools/gen-cond-macros.py merges
# One `<header>\t<macro>` per row.  The generator measures the value with the same clang
# invocation it uses for the config.h dump (`#include <config.h>` then `#include "<header>"`
# on the frozen include paths), so a row cannot go stale silently: a header that stops
# defining the macro is reported, and a wrong value shows up as a disagreement in
# tools/check-cond-eval.py before the file joins the verified list (PORTING.md P-66).
# || defined HAVE_ITIMERSPEC)` -> `# define PROFILER_CPU_SUPPORT`.  Both SIGPROF (27) and
# HAVE_SETITIMER (1) are in the config.h table, PROFILING is not, so the macro is defined and
# profiler.c's whole CPU-profiler region (C 343-524, C 699-712) is live text - without this
# row the evaluator called it dead and the gate rejected the port's `defsubr`s as
